item.title: Putin quer recrutar 300 mil novos soldados, afirma Zelenskiy
item.description: A Ucrânia acredita que a Rússia esteja planejando recrutar mais 300 mil soldados para seu esforço de guerra após as eleições parlamentares russas em meados de setembro, afirmou o presidente ucraniano Volodymyr Zelenskiy.
item.dc:creator: Max Hunder, Dan Peleschuk
item.content:encoded: A Ucrânia acredita que a Rússia esteja planejando recrutar mais 300 mil soldados para seu esforço de guerra após as eleições parlamentares russas em meados de setembro, afirmou o presidente ucraniano Volodymyr Zelenskiy. As forças de Moscou estão avançando em uma ofensiva para capturar o restante da região industrializada de Donbas, no leste da Ucrânia, onde suas tropas têm avançado a um custo que, segundo Kiev, é muito alto. Em declarações à imprensa divulgadas neste domingo, Zelenskiy disse que a Rússia poderia chamar de volta mais soldados em 2027 para atingir uma meta total de 500 mil, parte do que ele descreveu como uma “mobilização periférica” voltada para as regiões mais remotas da Rússia. “Acreditamos que isso não ocorrerá nas cidades centrais”, disse ele. “Mas não acho que eles consigam esconder isso muito bem.” As eleições parlamentares na Rússia estão marcadas para os dias 18 a 20 de setembro. Enquanto os combates se intensificam em torno da cidade estratégica de Kostiantynivka, Zelenskiy afirmou que a Rússia está perdendo um número “máximo” de soldados em sua tentativa de avançar para o chamado cinturão de fortalezas das cidades do leste da Ucrânia. Ele também comemorou os recentes avanços das tropas de Kiev no sudeste da Ucrânia, acrescentando que a extensão do território ocupado pela Rússia e liberado pelas forças ucranianas em 2026 seria igual. RÚSSIA AUMENTA PRODUÇÃO DE MÍSSEIS, AFIRMA ZELENSKIY A Rússia está reforçando sua ofensiva no campo de batalha com uma guerra aérea cada vez mais intensa contra cidades ucranianas, agravada por uma escassez crítica de mísseis interceptadores Patriot de fabricação norte-americana. Zelenskiy disse que os 264 interceptores que a Ucrânia espera receber em 2026 representam uma queda significativa em relação a 2025, quando a Ucrânia recebeu 364, e a 2023, quando recebeu 675. Ele acrescentou que a Rússia tem como objetivo desenvolver capacidade para produzir até 1.300 mísseis balísticos por ano. Ao longo do verão, a Ucrânia intensificou uma campanha de ataques com drones contra a infraestrutura econômica russa, incluindo refinarias de petróleo e armazéns de varejistas online, buscando destruir infraestruturas que, segundo ela, são fundamentais para o esforço de guerra da Rússia. O presidente russo, Vladimir Putin, afirmou em declarações no sábado que Kiev havia aberto a “caixa de Pandora” ao atacar alvos econômicos, dizendo que a Rússia retaliaria contra os “setores econômicos mais sensíveis” da Ucrânia.

item.title: England's Carse being investigated after incident, says ECB
item.description: England fast bowler Brydon Carse is being investigated over an incident in Derby on Saturday night, the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: England fast bowler Brydon Carse is being investigated over an incident in Derby on Saturday night, the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) said on Sunday. "We are aware of an incident which is reported to have taken place in Derby last night and we are currently investigating," an ECB spokesperson said. "We will provide a further update when possible." Videos circulating on social media appear to show the Durham bowler in handcuffs being led away from a club by police officers. Carse is part of England's squad for the second test against Pakistan starting next week at Lord's. He was not on England duty at the time of the alleged incident after being an unused member of the squad for the first test which England won comfortably at Headingley. The investigation comes five days after England's returning test captain Joe Root spoke of the players being "really good role models and human beings" after a series of incidents and accusations of a drinking culture. Controversy has followed England around in recent times with off-field issues during last winter’s tours, including Harry Brook being fined £30,000 ($40,908) following an altercation with a bouncer in Wellington as well as reports of drinking during a mid-Ashes trip to Noosa. This summer Ben Stokes broke a team curfew along with Gus Atkinson, with the pair dropped from the second test against New Zealand at the Oval. Former test captain Stokes eventually announced his retirement from international cricket while Brendon McCullum was sacked as test coach. The ECB would not confirm whether Carse was still in the squad for the second test against Pakistan. Reuters has contacted Carse's county side Durham to request comment from the player. In 2024, South Africa-born Carse was suspended from cricket for three months for historic betting offences. ($1 = 0.7334 pounds)

item.title: Robôs podem correr mais rápido que humanos, mas será que conseguem conectar um cabo?
item.description: Os robôs humanóides da China demonstraram que conseguem correr mais rápido do que os humanos mais velozes.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Baptista, Xihao Jiang, Qiaoyi Li
item.content:encoded: Os robôs humanóides da China demonstraram que conseguem correr mais rápido do que os humanos mais velozes. Agora vem o verdadeiro teste: será que eles também conseguem lidar com operações de embalagem e armazenamento, ao mesmo tempo em que realizam com confiabilidade tarefas de precisão, como conectar cabos, destinadas a avaliar sua capacidade de trabalhar como humanos em tarefas menos chamativas? Os Jogos Mundiais de Robôs Humanóides, com duração de cinco dias, que começaram no sábado em Pequim, combinam provas inspiradas em esportes humanos com outras projetadas para testar os robôs em fábricas, restaurantes e escritórios simulados, bem como em situações de emergência. Os jogos, amplamente divulgados pela mídia estatal chinesa, contam com 51 provas, incluindo 30 competições esportivas e 21 provas baseadas em cenários. Mais de 40% exigem que os robôs operem de forma totalmente autônoma, de acordo com a Huawei, parceira tecnológica dos jogos. No sábado, dois robôs correram mais rápido do que o recorde mundial de Usain Bolt, de 9,58 segundos, nos 100 metros rasos. Isso representou uma melhoria significativa em relação a 2025, quando o tempo do robô vencedor era superior a 20 segundos. A frenagem foi um problema, já que as máquinas bateram com força em um tapete grosso que os organizadores colocaram vários metros após a linha de chegada. Outro humanóide, do mesmo modelo do campeão dos 100 metros, correu 400 metros em 39,7 segundos, mais rápido que o recorde mundial do sul-africano Wayde van Niekerk, de 43,03 segundos. “A intensidade é maior do que no ano passado, o que exige muito da gestão da bateria e da capacidade de dissipação térmica do robô”, disse o espectador e investidor em robótica Xu Qiaosheng. “Isso tem enorme importância para o desenvolvimento do setor industrial da China.” Os robôs competirão em cabo de guerra e levantamento de peso, enquanto o tai chi e o “pitch-pot” — em que os competidores lançam varas em forma de flecha dentro de um vaso de gargalo estreito — darão um toque futurista aos esportes tradicionais chineses. GRANDES DESAFIOS EM PEQUENAS IMPERFEIÇÕES Além do espetáculo, os testes mais reveladores podem surgir quando os robôs se deparam com as pequenas imperfeições do mundo físico: um cabo em um ângulo errado, um objeto fora de alcance, uma embalagem que se desloca ou um passo em falso. Isso testa se os robôs são capazes de identificar objetos, posicionar com precisão suas mãos e corpos, aplicar força controlada e se recuperar de erros sem intervenção humana. O diretor executivo da Lumos Robotics, Yu Chao, disse que os jogos podem ajudar a aprimorar o hardware e servir como vitrine para o setor. Mas Yu afirmou que o valor a longo prazo dependerá da resolução de problemas do mundo real. “Só quando ele conseguir funcionar nesses cenários finais é que terá valor real”, disse Yu. “Simplesmente correr e pular não melhora a eficiência.” Além de provas mais conhecidas, inspiradas nos esportes humanos, os robôs competirão em recarga de veículos elétricos, trabalho em restaurantes, atendimento a incidentes de emergência e competições de destreza manual. Há também provas de montagem industrial e carregamento de materiais. Um desafio de conexão de cabos é um teste de visão, alinhamento mecânico e controle de força. A Galbot, startup de robótica sediada em Pequim, anunciou que realizará uma partida autônoma de tênis com humanóides, na qual os robôs tentarão jogar em simples e em duplas, incluindo rastreamento da bola, saques e devoluções. Para Hua Rong, diretora de marketing da empresa de robótica Zeroth, o verdadeiro teste virá após o término das demonstrações. “A verdadeira competição será saber se, depois que o produto for vendido, ele realmente poderá resolver os problemas dos usuários”, disse ela.

item.title: Norris gana el Gran Premio de Países Bajos y Antonelli amplía su ventaja en la general
item.description: Lando Norris dio a McLaren su tercera victoria consecutiva en el Gran Premio de los Países Bajos el domingo, en una carrera llena de altibajos que tuvo que reiniciarse después de que el héroe local, Max Verstappen, sufrió un accidente en la primera vuelta.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: Lando Norris dio a McLaren su tercera victoria consecutiva en el Gran Premio de los Países Bajos el domingo, en una carrera llena de altibajos que tuvo que reiniciarse después de que el héroe local, Max Verstappen, sufrió un accidente en la primera vuelta. El líder del campeonato de Mercedes, Kimi Antonelli, terminó segundo y aumentó su ventaja en la clasificación, mientras que su compañero de equipo, George Russell, obedeció las órdenes de dejar pasar al italiano en los últimos compases de la carrera y luego se impuso a Lewis Hamilton, de Ferrari, para hacerse con el tercer puesto. La victoria de Norris es la segunda consecutiva del actual campeón del mundo, que salió primero en la grilla pero que tuvo que remontar a Antonelli en la reanudación, tras su victoria en Hungría el mes pasado. "Sigamos introduciendo mejoras. Sigamos mejorando el rendimiento. La lucha continúa. Sigamos adelante", dijo Norris, que ganó en Zandvoort en 2024 antes de que su compañero de equipo Oscar Piastri triunfara el año pasado. Todas las carreras de F1 disputadas en Zandvoort desde que el circuito volvió al calendario en 2021, tras una ausencia de 36 años, se han ganado desde la "pole", y la del domingo mantuvo la racha. Antonelli amplió su ventaja a 59 puntos sobre Russell y Hamilton, que ahora están empatados a 183 cada uno frente a los 242 del italiano de 19 años, tras 12 pruebas. "Con los neumáticos nuevos, me habría adelantado de todos modos, así que fue la decisión correcta", dijo Russell, ganador de la carrera sprint del sábado, sobre las órdenes de su equipo. "Simplemente estoy contento de estar en el podio. Hacía tiempo que no lo conseguía y, en general, ha sido un fin de semana muy bueno". Charles Leclerc, de Ferrari, terminó quinto; Piastri, sexto; y Liam Lawson, sustituto del lesionado Isack Hadjar, séptimo con Red Bull. Nico Hülkenberg fue octavo con Audi, mientras que Fernando Alonso volvió a meter a Aston Martin —con un motor Honda más potente— en los puntos al quedar noveno. Pierre Gasly se hizo con el décimo puesto para Alpine, propiedad de Renault.

item.title: Norris wins Dutch GP as Antonelli stretches his F1 lead
item.description: Lando Norris gave McLaren a third successive Dutch Grand Prix victory on Sunday in an intense race of shifting fortunes that had to be restarted after home hero Max Verstappen crashed on the opening lap.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: Lando Norris gave McLaren a third successive Dutch Grand Prix victory on Sunday in an intense race of shifting fortunes that had to be restarted after home hero Max Verstappen [USN:L6N44K03N TEXT:"crashed on the opening lap."] Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli finished second to increase his championship lead, with teammate George Russell obeying orders to let the Italian -- on fresher tyres -- through late in the race and then holding off Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton for third. The win was a second in a row for reigning world champion Norris, who started on pole position but had to fight back after losing the lead to Antonelli at the restart, following victory in Hungary last month. He is now fourth overall, 83 points adrift of Antonelli, and still hopeful of closing the gap. "Let's keep bringing upgrades. Let's keep bringing performance. The fight is still on. Let's keep going," said Norris, who won at Zandvoort in 2024 before teammate Oscar Piastri triumphed last year, still the Australian's most recent win. FINAL LAP IN F1 FOR ZANDVOORT CIRCUIT Every F1 race at Zandvoort since the circuit returned to the calendar in 2021 after a 36-year absence has been won from pole, and Sunday's will keep it that way as the [USN:L6N44J02J TEXT:"last for the foreseeable future."] Antonelli stretched his lead to 59 points over Russell and Hamilton, now tied on 183 each to the 19-year-old Italian's 242, after 12 rounds. "With the new tyres, he would have overtaken anyway so it was the right decision," said Russell, who won Saturday's sprint but lost out to Antonelli at the first start on Sunday, of the team orders. "Just happy to be standing on the podium. It's been a little while for me and a strong weekend overall." Ferrari's Charles Leclerc finished fifth with Piastri sixth and Liam Lawson, a stand-in for injured Isack Hadjar, seventh for Red Bull. Nico Hulkenberg was eighth for Audi, after almost hitting his spinning teammate Gabriel Bortoleto on a damp opening lap, with Fernando Alonso more than doubling Aston Martin's points tally so far this season with ninth -- an immediate result for Honda's engine upgrade. Pierre Gasly took 10th for Renault-owned Alpine. ONE CHANCE TO MAKE IT HAPPEN After various changes of lead through the pitstops, Norris passed Antonelli on track with 18 laps to go after he had pitted seven laps later than the Italian and made his fresher tyres count in a champion's drive. "I probably had one chance to make it happen and I made the most of it," he said. Norris then also passed Hamilton, who had inherited the lead but was yet to make his final stop after earlier chafing over the team radio at being held up behind Leclerc, with Antonelli following through. Hamilton pitted when a virtual safety car was deployed after Haas's Esteban Ocon stopped on track, with Antonelli also seizing a chance for fresh tyres while Russell and Norris stayed out. He came back out 12 seconds behind Norris. "Do you think we need to take it (the stop)? I'm a bit worried now," Norris said over the radio but the opportunity was in any case gone and the Briton instead showed his pace by lapping faster on older tyres than his rival. Russell was told to 'invert the cars', coded speak for letting his teammate through, and he did so after briefly questioning the order. "We've lost a double podium here," said the Briton as Hamilton closed right up, before another virtual safety car helped Russell get to the finish ahead. Both Mercedes drivers exchanged friendly gestures after the finish. Norris crossed the line 11.5 seconds clear of Antonelli. "I made it tough for myself today but a good race. Well fought. Probably one of my better wins. We had to fight for it," said the McLaren driver.

item.title: Late Gvardiol strike earns Maresca winning start, Liverpool snatch last-gasp draw
item.description: Manchester City's post-Pep Guardiola era began with Josko Gvardiol's stoppage-time winner earning a 2-1 victory at home to Bournemouth in Enzo Maresca's first Premier League game in charge on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Lori Ewing
item.content:encoded: Manchester City's post-Pep Guardiola era began with Josko Gvardiol's stoppage-time winner earning a 2-1 victory at home to Bournemouth in Enzo Maresca's first Premier League game in charge on Sunday. New Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola also required some even later intervention as Dominik Szoboszlai's last-gasp penalty salvaged his side a 2-2 draw at Newcastle United, another club beginning the campaign with a new man at the helm. An unpredictable opening weekend of the Premier League season also saw Unai Emery's Aston Villa thrashed 4-0 at Brighton and Hove Albion, all the goals arriving before halftime. Maresca's reign began with a chastening Community Shield defeat by champions Arsenal last week and City were in danger of another loss after Marcus Tavernier slammed home a 26th-minute shot from a low ball across the area by Evanilson. City huffed and puffed in response with newly-shaven Erling Haaland missing several chances to equalise. But Marc Guehi, playing as a deep midfielder rather than in defence, hauled City level in the 84th minute when he rose to power home a header from a Rayan Cherki corner. Gvardiol sparked wild celebrations with a close-range finish in the 91st minute that was initially ruled offside but allowed after a VAR overturn. It was tough on Bournemouth and Iraola's replacement Marco Rose as the south coast club's 18-match record unbeaten league run stretching back to January came to an end. 'THE JOY OF THE THREE POINTS' Maresca, who was welcomed with a banner unfurled in the East Stand, said it had been a perfect day despite the scare. "I was glad when it was over also, to give them the joy of the three points. It was quite emotional and the perfect day," Guardiola's former assistant at City said. "It's a game that we deserved to win. A game probably you don't need to win in the last eight minutes for the amount of chances we had." Fans of Newcastle and Liverpool were united in their show of respect for Kevin Keegan at St James' Park after the death of their shared hero, who passed away aged 75 in July. An emotional pre-match tribute to Keegan included a huge tifo depicting the man who scored 100 goals and won seven major trophies with Liverpool and who later played for and managed Newcastle, where he was known as King Kev. Both sets of players wore warm-up shirts bearing Keegan's name and famous No.7. "It was probably the best fixture to happen for the first game of the season after what happened," Iraola, who replaced Arne Slot at the end of last season, said. "It's good that both supporters can remember him like they did today." As so often happened when the two sides met during Keegan's managerial career at Newcastle, the game had a dramatic finale as Szoboszlai robbed the home side of what would have been a great start under their new manager Matthias Jaissle. Anthony Elanga put the hosts ahead in the fifth minute only for Cody Gakpo to level early in the second half. Joe Willock immediately curled Newcastle back ahead having come off the bench but Lewis Hall was adjudged to have bundled over Victor Munoz and Szoboszlai lashed home the penalty in the ninth minute of stoppage time. 'THINGS TO IMPROVE' "I've liked a lot of the things I've seen from the team today," Iraola said. "Definitely things to improve but I've liked the energy, especially the players coming from the bench. I think we finished the game quite strong physically." Villa have seen their Europa League-winning side dismantled over the summer with the likes of Morgan Rogers, Lucas Digne, Youri Tielemans and Ezri Konsa all sold and the size of Emery's rebuilding job was exposed in the south coast sunshine. They capitulated before halftime, conceding four goals and having new signing Joao Gomes sent off. An own goal by Victor Lindelof after eight minutes was followed by a second from Maxim De Cuyper. Jack Hinshelwood's double inside two minutes had Brighton in dreamland and while Villa did show some character in the second half it was a worrying start to the campaign. The Villa exodus could continue with striker Ollie Watkins left out of the squad on Sunday. Asked why, Emery said: "Ask him. I only can answer it by silence." The opening round of fixtures concludes on Monday with Chelsea at local rivals Fulham.

item.content:encoded: Raízen posted the transcript of its Q1 2026/27 crop-year earnings call attended by CEO Nelson Gomes, CFO Lorival Luz, IR officer Phillipe Casale. Fuel Distribution Argentina reclassified to Discontinued Operations as the June 4 sale process advances; non-cash held-for-sale revaluation booked. Gomes flagged record Fuel Distribution margins as partly war-driven and temporary; expects margins above last year but below this quarter. Casale cited R$ 3.6 billion operating cash flow; Capex down 33%; net loss driven by higher financial expenses and discontinued-operations effects. Luz said leverage allocation between Fuel Distribution and Sugar/Ethanol remains undecided; focus on completing the plan by March, separation by December. item.title: Eleven bodies recovered after boat carrying migrants sinks off Tunisia
item.description: Eleven bodies have been recovered by Tunisia's coastguard after a boat carrying Tunisian migrants sank at the weekend en route to Italy, with three others still unaccounted for, the National Guard said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Eleven bodies have been recovered by Tunisia's coastguard after a boat carrying Tunisian migrants [USN:L1N44J00D TEXT:"sank at the weekend"] en route to Italy, with three others still unaccounted for, the National Guard said on Sunday. Coastguard, military and civil protection teams, backed by two helicopters, continued to search for the missing. The boat, which set off early on Thursday with 15 mostly young people on board, sank off the Tunisian coast, and so far only one person was rescued alive, the head of a migrant rights group said on Saturday. The man who survived said he had been adrift at sea for 48 hours before being rescued by a commercial vessel. Among those on board were seven members of the same family and a man with his pregnant wife, the head of the Tunisian Observatory for Human Rights told Reuters. All of the migrants were from the Ben Guerdane area in southeastern Tunisia, and dozens of young people gathered late on Saturday in the town near the Libyan border to demand that search operations be accelerated. Police fired teargas to disperse the protesters. The central Mediterranean route from the North African coast is one of the world's deadliest migration routes, used by migrants from Africa and the Middle East seeking to reach Europe, often in overcrowded or unseaworthy boats. Human Rights Watch, Amnesty International and dozens of other human rights and humanitarian groups said in a statement last month that a migration agreement between Tunisia and the European Union had fuelled and normalised [USN:L1N3I80RQ TEXT:"serious abuses"] against migrants and asylum seekers in Tunisia. The groups called on the EU to suspend funding for migration and border-control activities involving Tunisian security forces.

item.title: Israeli airstrikes in Gaza kill two people, including 4-year-old boy, medics say
item.description: Medics said flying debris and shrapnel that spread for dozens of metres around had wounded at least six people.
item.dc:creator: Nidal Al-Mughrabi
item.content:encoded: Two Israeli airstrikes in the Gaza Strip on Sunday killed at least two people, including a four-year-old boy, and wounded seven others, Palestinian health officials said, as Israel warned it would intensify strikes after what it said were launches of balloons, drones and kites from Gaza toward Israel. One of the strikes hit a building in Zawayda town in the centre of the enclave and followed a warning by the Israeli army for the owners of the property to leave the area, residents said. Medics said flying debris and shrapnel that spread for dozens of metres around had wounded at least six people, including the four-year-old, Mohammad Abdel-Salam Taha, who was later pronounced dead at hospital. "There is no ceasefire, there is nothing," said Abu Ahmed, a displaced Palestinian who was sheltering close to the building, which the airstrike reduced to a pile of mangled steel and concrete. "We want solutions, we want to live in peace," he said. The second airstrike took place in the nearby Nuseirat refugee camp, the health officials said. Israel's military said it was looking into both strikes. ISRAEL TARGETS HAMAS DESPITE CEASEFIRE An October 2025 U.S.-backed [USN:L2N3VR084 TEXT:"ceasefire"] halted major fighting in the shattered territory, but it failed to end strikes by the Israeli military, which it said aimed to thwart attacks by Hamas and other Gaza militants. The military said in a statement late on Saturday that it had struck and killed a senior Hamas militant, Sharif Al-Hasnat, in the city of Deir Al-Balah. It said he was leading efforts to restore Hamas' "underground infrastructure". Hamas accuses Israel of violating the ceasefire and undermining efforts to implement a broader plan by U.S. President [USN:L1N44H0JU TEXT:"Donald Trump"] to end the Gaza conflict, which also includes Israeli withdrawals and Hamas disarmament. More than 1,280 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza since the ceasefire took effect last October, according to Gazan health officials, while the Israeli military says four Israeli soldiers have been killed. Israel has reported the launch of drones, balloons and kites from the Gaza Strip toward Israel. Following a situation assessment on Sunday, it warned Hamas it would intensify strikes in Gaza and order civilians to evacuate areas if the launches didn't stop immediately, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office said in a statement. Senior Hamas official Basem Naim dismissed Israel’s warning, writing on X that children launch the kites “in search of their innocent childhood amid the rubble.” WEST BANK VIOLENCE In the Israeli-occupied West Bank, an Israeli man was stabbed and wounded by a suspect believed to be a Palestinian man, police and the Israeli military said. Security camera footage distributed by the military showed a man waiting by a vehicle next to a main highway near Jericho before stabbing the Israeli man when he approached his parked car. The suspect fled on foot and Israeli soldiers were searching for him, the military said. Elsewhere in the West Bank, health officials said Israeli forces had shot and killed a 14-year-old boy, Islam Ajjouri, during a raid into Askar refugee camp near Nablus. The Israeli military said it was looking into the incident. The West Bank, home to 3 million Palestinians and some 500,000 settlers, has seen a rise in settler violence and seizures of land and resources. U.N. bodies and most countries view the settlements as illegal under international law regarding military occupations. Israel disputes this and it cites biblical and historical ties to the land.

item.title: Iran says new sanctions threatened by 'desperate' US will fail
item.description: Iran's economy is under huge pressure from sanctions and thousands have died in airstrikes since February.
item.dc:creator: Elwely Elwelly, Menna Alaaeldin
item.content:encoded: Iran's foreign minister dismissed the threat of new U.S. sanctions as a sign of desperation on Sunday and said the expected new measures would fail to defeat Tehran. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who is due to hold a press conference at 2 p.m. EDT (1800 GMT) on Monday, has threatened to impose "[USN:L6N44H0X1 TEXT:"the toughest sanctions in history"]" on Iran. Iran's economy is already under huge pressure from international sanctions, its infrastructure has been hit repeatedly and thousands of people have been killed in airstrikes on the Islamic Republic since the U.S. and Israel launched attacks on February 28. But Tehran remains defiant after nearly six months of war and has brought shipping to a virtual standstill in the Strait of Hormuz, refusing to allow unauthorized oil tankers to transit a waterway that is vital for global oil shipments. The effective blockade of the strait has pushed up [USN:L1N44I027 TEXT:"global oil prices"]. Describing what he said were "repetitive scenarios", Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said in a video posted on Telegram: "The fact that they (U.S. leaders) have moved on from military operations ... to bring up the same old plans shows that they are desperate." He said Washington must speak to Iran respectfully to find "a solution based on justice and honour." "We have never been afraid. All of their actions - whether blockades or other military moves they have made - have failed, and this new issue of theirs will fail as well," he said. U.S. President Donald Trump has warned of economic consequences against any country that provides "any type of lifeline to Iran" and Bessent has urged cooperation with Washington by [USN:L6N44H0PZ TEXT:"China"], which buys more than 80% of Iran's shipped oil, according to 2025 data from analytics firm Kpler. China has urged diplomacy. PAKISTAN'S ARMY CHIEF TO VISIT TEHRAN Iran said [USN:L1N44K01W TEXT:"Pakistan's army chief"], Asim Munir, would visit Tehran on Monday as part of efforts to restore peace and security in the region, but gave few details. Pakistan has been mediating in the conflict and a Pakistani government source said Munir would touch on recent developments including the U.S. threat of new sanctions. Trump said on Friday that Washington was observing "what happens" in the conflict. "They would love to make a deal, but they're not ready to make the right deal, in my opinion," Trump said of Iran. U.S. attacks have severely diminished Iran's economy and devastated its navy and air force, but Tehran maintains enough missile and drone capability to impede oil tanker traffic and attack regional rivals. Iranian Parliament speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf said on Saturday that Tehran had received "numerous messages" from neighbouring countries about establishing new regional security arrangements and economic cooperation. Qalibaf did not say which countries he was referring to. He accused the U.S. of endangering the security of its allies in the region for the sake of Israel, adding that an independent, "homegrown" regional order would deliver peace and security. Trump has yet to achieve objectives he set at the start of the war such as dismantling Iran's nuclear programme — the state of which remains uncertain given that U.N. inspectors have been shut out since 2025 — and creating conditions for Iranians to overthrow their clerical rulers. While Iran remains defiant, President Masoud Pezeshkian has also called for a diplomatic solution. "It would be better to end the war today, when we are powerful and have dignity, and the whole world acknowledges our victory and emphasizes that America, contrary to all regulations, attacked our schools, hospitals, and infrastructure and is hated in the world," the ISNA news agency quoted him as saying on Friday.

item.title: Trump caps summer of US 250th birthday at IndyCar race through Washington
item.description: The race was expected to draw roughly 200,000 spectators; tickets were free.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Bogage
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump capped celebrations of the U.S. 250th anniversary with a first-of-its-kind [USN:L6N44318W TEXT:"auto race"] through the streets of Washington, closing a summer of sports and spectacle as drivers sped past the capital's iconic landmarks. IndyCar's Freedom 250 Grand Prix zoomed through the National Mall, down historic Pennsylvania Avenue and around the National Archives, in the marquee event on Sunday afternoon. The race was expected to draw roughly 200,000 spectators, officials said, and tickets were free. Passes to private trackside clubs sold for $5,000. TRUMP TAKES A LAP, WAVES THE GREEN FLAG Trump 's motorcade took an honorary loop around the race course before he waved the green flag to officially start the 250-mile (402-km) race at about 1:18 p.m. ET (1718 GMT). Although the green flag at IndyCar events typically is waved atop a tower at the start/finish line, Trump remained in his presidential box for Sunday's start. The race is the latest in a series of sporting events Trump has used to celebrate the country and his second term, even as his approval rating has dropped to the [USN:L6N44E0VE TEXT:"lowest point"] since he returned to the White House in January 2025, and the U.S. is embroiled in a war with Iran. He opened the summer with a professional [USN:L6N42J12W TEXT:"mixed martial arts bout"] on the South Lawn of the White House, then presented the trophy to FIFA World Cup champion Spain a month later. Earlier in August, he appeared at the “Patriot Games,” a cross between a game show and track meet for high school athletes, televised on sports network ESPN. For Trump, the events have served to raise his profile, both domestically and globally. The UFC fight card was streamed internationally, and during the World Cup trophy presentation, he lingered at mid-pitch while the Spanish team hoisted the trophy. The unusual setting for an IndyCar race, with the U.S. Capitol and Smithsonian museums as the backdrop, was not lost on the drivers. "What an incredible place to do it," race winner Kyle Kirkwood told Fox Sports after his victory. RACE PLANS HAVE FACED CRITICISM The Washington race faced its share of criticism. The track was originally set to run through the grounds of the U.S. Capitol, but the proposal required lawmakers' approval and stalled in Congress. Advertising is prohibited on Capitol grounds, and the race cars, with their dozens of corporate sponsors, along with trackside billboards, would have run afoul of those regulations. Trump instead issued an executive order commanding Transportation Department officials to draw up a course that did not require congressional signoff. Officials [USN:S0N43A04H TEXT:"paused air traffic"] at Washington's Ronald Reagan National Airport for three hours at midday on Sunday to accommodate the IndyCar event's military flyovers, including one featuring a Boeing 747 jet often used as Air Force One, and another including what appeared to be a B-2 stealth bomber. The city's police closed major thoroughfares downtown due to pedestrian activity and security procedures. Race officials said the city's roads will not need much refurbishment before or after the race, in which drivers are expected to reach 185 miles per hour (298 km per hour) on the Pennsylvania Avenue straightaway.

item.title: Norway to give over $9 billion to Ukraine in 2027
item.description: Norway plans to give another 85 billion Norwegian crowns ($9.2 billion) in financial support to Ukraine in the 2027 fiscal year, in line with the amount given in 2026, the Nordic country's government said in a statement on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Norway plans to give another 85 billion Norwegian crowns ($9.2 billion) in financial support to Ukraine in the 2027 fiscal year, in line with the amount given in 2026, the Nordic country's government said in a statement on Sunday. Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Stoere and leaders from across the Nordic and Baltic region are visiting Kyiv on Sunday in a show of support for Ukraine in the war with Russia. Norway's donation will be for both military and humanitarian spending, Stoere was quoted as saying in the text of a speech released by the government in Oslo. "Supporting and rebuilding Ukraine is not assistance alone. It is an investment in Europe's own security," Stoere said. Separately, Finland and Ukraine have signed a letter of intent on manufacturing and developing unmanned systems in Finland and memorandum of understanding for a joint venture to produce uncrewed surface vessels, among other documents, Zelenskiy's office said on X. In comments published on Saturday, Russian President [USN:L6N44J044 TEXT:"Vladimir Putin"] said that Kyiv had opened a "Pandora's box" with its strikes on Russian economic targets and that Moscow would hit back at Ukraine's "most sensitive economic sectors". Russia and Ukraine are both ramping up drone campaigns aiming to cripple each other's economic infrastructure, often striking targets far beyond the frontlines of the war started by Moscow, as fighting on the battlefield grinds toward the 4-1/2-year mark. ($1 = 9.2875 Norwegian crowns)

item.title: New pro-presidential party wins large majority in Kazakh election, exit polls show
item.description: A newly formed pro-government party won a large majority in a snap parliamentary election in Kazakhstan on Sunday, three different exit polls showed, in a result set to cement President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's power over the country, a major energy and minerals exporter.
item.dc:creator: Felix Light
item.content:encoded: A newly formed pro-government party won a large majority in a snap parliamentary election in Kazakhstan on Sunday, three different exit polls showed, in a result set to cement President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's power over the country, a major energy and minerals exporter. The exit polls, which were published on Kazakh state media, showed the Adilet party winning between 70% and 72% of the vote, with a turnout of more than 74%. The exit polls said four small opposition parties also won seats, though they too are widely seen as ultimately loyal to Tokayev. The victory of Adilet, which was formed earlier this year by the president's top aides and which swiftly absorbed previous long-ruling party Amanat, is likely to deepen Tokayev's control over the country at the expense of figures more closely linked to his predecessor, Nursultan Nazarbayev. A former Soviet diplomat and top United Nations official, Tokayev has led Central Asia's largest economy since 2019, keeping warm relations with the West, Russia and China. Sunday's [USN:L1N44H092 TEXT:"election"] was triggered by the adoption of a new constitution earlier this year, which streamlines parliament from two chambers into one. Kazakhstan's Supreme Court said last month the new constitution allowed Tokayev to run for a fresh seven-year term. Tokayev took office as the chosen successor of Nazarbayev, Kazakhstan's founding president, who ruled from 1991 to 2019. He broke with Nazarbayev after a 2022 bout of unrest that he has cast as a coup attempt by Nazarbayev allies. Voting in the capital, Astana, Tokayev told journalists it was too early to say whether he would seek another term. He also said he would announce his choice of vice president, an office created under the new constitution, in the next seven to 10 days, and that his choice would be a "well-known" person.

item.title: Peace Through Strength, Taiwan President Says on China Battle Anniversary
item.description: By Ben Blanchard and Yi-Chin Lee Peace can only be secured through strength and not even an inch of territory can be sacrificed, Taiwan President Lai Ching-te said on Sunday, visiting a sensitive frontline island to mark a key battle with Chinese forces almost seven …
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded:
By Ben Blanchard and Yi-Chin Lee

Peace can only be secured through strength and not even an inch of territory can be sacrificed, Taiwan President Lai Ching-te said on Sunday, visiting a sensitive frontline island to mark a key battle with Chinese forces almost seven decades ago.

Taiwan has controlled the Kinmen and Matsu islands, which lie just off the Chinese coast, since the Republic of China government fled to Taipei in 1949 after losing a civil war with Mao Zedong’s communists. No peace treaty or armistice has ever been signed.

In heavy rain, Lai laid a wreath and bowed at a memorial park for the 68th anniversary of the 1958 clash with Chinese forces, known as the start of the second Taiwan Strait crisis — the last time Taiwanese and Chinese forces battled on a large scale.

Addressing veterans later, Lai expressed gratitude to those who “stood united and fought a bloody battle to repel Communist totalitarian aggression”.

“Our resolve to unite in defending national sovereignty and safeguarding peace across the Taiwan Strait must never waver,” Lai said. “Peace has never simply fallen from the sky.”

The 1958 battle proves “that peace is secured through strength,” he said, adding it was necessary to maintain “the spirit of never yielding an inch” of Taiwan, Kinmen and another group of islands, while continuously boosting military spending.

China’s Taiwan Affairs Office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Close to China

China views democratically governed Taiwan as its own territory and has repeatedly denounced Lai as a “separatist”. He rejects Beijing’s sovereignty, saying only Taiwan’s people can decide their future, but has also offered talks with China.

Kinmen at its closest is less than 2 km (1.2 miles) from Chinese-controlled territory. In the 1958 battle, Chinese forces began more than a month of bombardment of Kinmen, along with Matsu, including naval and air battles, seeking to force them into submission.

Taiwan fought back with support from the United States, though the crisis ended in a stalemate. Taiwan observes August 23 every year as the date it fended off the Chinese attack.

China’s coast guard has since early 2024 conducted regular “law enforcement” patrols around Kinmen in Taiwan-controlled waters, to Taipei’s anger.

Referring to those patrols and other Chinese tactics, Lai said that for 68 years China had not stopped its “ambitions for external expansion for even a single day”, bringing “unease” across the Indo-Pacific.

Taiwan’s planned defence spending next year will exceed T$1 trillion ($30 billion) for the first time, the government announced on Thursday, and Lai said he hoped for strong support for the budget.

($1 = 31.8250 Taiwan dollars)

(Reporting by Ben Blanchard and Yi-Chin Lee)

item.title: Syria foreign minister sees Israel security talks resuming despite no trust
item.description: Damascus' priority is to halt Israeli attacks, Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani said, adding that "We do not trust Israel currently."
item.dc:creator: Tom Perry, Feras Dalatey
item.content:encoded: Syria expects negotiations to resume soon with Israel over a security deal it hopes will lead to Israel's withdrawal from Syrian land, a top Syrian minister said, urging Israel to seize a "historic opportunity" as the door for diplomacy is open. In a Reuters interview in Damascus on Saturday, days after[USN:L6N44F0E4 TEXT:" Israel bombed a Syrian airbase,"] Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani also stressed that Damascus' priority is to halt Israeli attacks, saying confidence-building steps were needed in this direction. Washington has been seeking to forge a security deal between Israel and the government of Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa, a new U.S. ally in the Middle East, for over a year. But it has proven elusive as Israel has sent troops into Syrian territory and attacked government assets, citing threats to its security. Shaibani said negotiations over the security agreement had been frozen since the start of the Iran war, but he expected them to restart. Contact between Syria and Israel was cut after the airbase strike, he said. "We believe there should be contact, especially with a party that constantly threatens the security of Syria. But if this contact doesn’t bring results, then we don’t need it," Shaibani said. "We do not trust Israel currently." The Israeli prime minister's office did not respond to a request for comment. U.S. PRESSURE Sharaa has said Syria poses no threat to other countries, with Damascus focused on rebuilding from 14 years of war. Israeli officials have talked about a range of potential dangers in Syria since Bashar al-Assad was toppled, with some describing the new rulers as barely disguised jihadists last year, even as Sharaa forged close U.S. ties. In the days after Assad fell in 2024, Israel seized territory in southwest Syria, citing the need to safeguard its citizens against attack, and [USN:S8N3MY01K TEXT:"bombed scores"] of Syrian military sites. "Israel has tried to maintain its security through brute force and it hasn’t succeeded" anywhere, Shaibani said. "I believe negotiations will resume soon." No date has been set. "The U.S. is trying continuously to put pressure on Israel to return to the dialogue table," he added. Asked how optimistic he was, Shaibani said: "It’s very hard to bet on Israel." But Syria had "very great hope" of building stable relationships with its neighbours. "Syria is extending its hand for understandings, for peace, for diplomacy" and regional stability. SYRIA DID NOT SEE ISRAELI WILL TO MAKE DEAL [USN:L1N44H05K TEXT:"Tensions over Syria"] were brought into focus on Tuesday when Israel bombed the Abu al-Duhur airbase, saying Damascus was about to allow Turkish forces to deploy there. Syria and Turkey denied the claim. Shaibani said Syria respected Israel's security concerns but that Israel must respect those of Syria, including Israel's use of its airspace, Israeli raids and arrests in the south. He said that around the beginning of the year, the sides had "agreed on paper to almost everything" regarding a security deal that would require Israel to stop attacking Syria and was tied to its withdrawal from territory seized after Assad fell. The deal would include several security zones in Syrian territory near the Israeli border, including a buffer zone where only the United Nations would be present, and others where Syrian forces would deploy in varying degrees of force. But he said Israel had sought to evade implementation, adding: "We did not see they had the real will to reach an agreement." GOLAN HEIGHTS Syria and Israel have technically been in a state of war since 1948. Israel seized the Golan Heights from Syria in a 1967 war. The priority now is to "stop Israeli aggression even before reaching a security agreement", Shaibani said. "Then perhaps we can open the topics of peace and the Golan." U.S. special envoy for Syria Tom Barrack said on Tuesday that Washington was working to establish [USN:L8N44F1A3 TEXT:"a mechanism"] to prevent conflict among Israel, Turkey and Syria. Shaibani said there was no agreement yet on the mechanism, which he said must stop attacks and pave the way for the security deal rather than "entrenching ... Israeli occupation." The U.S. State Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Shaibani said Israel had bombed Abu al-Duhur even after Syria [USN:L1N44H02A TEXT:"conveyed a message"] that it would not be a Turkish base. Syria draws on Turkish support in military training and cooperation, he said, noting that this was also the case with Jordan, Saudi Arabia and others. Damascus was thankful for Turkey’s support in rebuilding its military “and we won’t forgo support", he said.

item.title: フィギュアスケート＝「りくりゅう」が婚約を発表、ミラノ五輪で日本勢初のペア金
item.description:
Yuka Obayashi
[東京 ２３日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Yuka Obayashi

[東京 ２３日 ロイター] - ミラノ・コルティナ冬季五輪で金メダルを獲得した「りくりゅう」の愛称で知られるフィギュアスケートのペア、三浦璃来と木原龍一が２３日、婚約を発表した。

二人はインスタグラムに、木原がスケートリンクの上でひざまずき、三浦に指輪を差し出す写真を添えて「婚約しました」と投稿。「嬉しい時も、辛い時も、たくさんの時間を共に過ごし、支え合いながら歩んできました」とつづった。

投稿には、５時間足らずで１万４０００件以上の祝福メッセージが寄せられた。

三浦・木原ペアはミラノ・コルティナ冬季五輪のショートプログラム（ＳＰ）で５位と出遅れながら、フリーでは世界歴代最高の１５８．１３点をマークし、日本勢として同種目史上初となる金メダルを獲得。４月に引退を発表していた。

item.title: 台湾総統、力による平和を強調 中国との戦闘から68年で金門島訪問
item.description:
Ben Blanchard Yi-Chin Lee
[金門（台湾） ２３日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Ben Blanchard　Yi-Chin Lee

[金門（台湾）　２３日　ロイター] - 台湾の頼清徳総統は２３日、中国が台湾支配下の金門島を攻撃した１９５８年の第２次台湾海峡危機から６８年となるのに合わせて同島を訪問し、平和は力によってのみ守られるとして、台湾の領土を「一寸たりとも譲らない」と強調した。

頼氏は記念公園で献花後、退役軍人らを前に演説し、犠牲者への敬意を表明。「国家主権を守り、台湾海峡の平和を維持する決意は決して揺らいではならない。平和は自然に得られるものではない」と述べた。

第２次台湾海峡危機は５８年８月から１カ月余りにわたり、中国人民解放軍が台湾沖の金門島侵攻を企図して行った攻撃に台湾側が反撃して起きた戦闘で、中台間で最後の本格的な武力衝突となった。

台湾政府は、２０２７年度の国防予算案が初めて１兆台湾ドル（約５兆円）を超える見通しだと発表している。

item.title: Australia confirms first H5N1 bird flu case in local mammal
item.description: South Australian authorities confirmed the nation's first mammalian detection of the H5N1 virus in a long-nosed fur seal, which was found dead with no signs of injury.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

World

Australia confirms first H5N1 bird flu case in local mammal

South Australian authorities confirmed the nation's first mammalian detection of the H5N1 virus in a long-nosed fur seal, which was found dead with no signs of injury.

A test tube labelled "Bird Flu", eggs and a piece of paper in the colours of the Australian national flag are seen in this picture taken on Jan 14, 2023. (File photo: Reuters/Dado Ruvic)

FAST

SYDNEY: Australia on Sunday (Aug 23) confirmed its first case of H5N1 bird flu in a mammal, with the deadly virus found in a long-nosed fur seal in South Australia state. Australia has been grappling with rising cases of the highly pathogenic avian influenza after it landed in the country in June. The country's first mass seabird deaths from the virus occurred this month, marking an escalation of the outbreak that began after the virus was first detected in migratory seabirds before spreading to native species. South Australian authorities confirmed the nation's first mammalian detection in the seal, found at the coastal town of Beachport, about 310km south of Adelaide, the state capital. The seal, one of an estimated population of 100,000 in the state's waters, was found dead with no signs of injury, the authorities said.

Its death "does not appear to be associated with other sick or dead marine mammals," federal Agriculture Minister Julie Collins said in televised remarks. "Once the H5 bird flu is spreading in the natural environment it is not possible to avoid significant losses." Australia was the last continent to report bird flu, although the virus was detected in late 2025 on the sub-Antarctic territory of Heard Island. More than 13,000 baby seals were killed by the virus on the island, according to local media. Seals are at high risk of contracting the virus, said South Australia's chief veterinary officer, Skye Fruean, because they live very near wild birds on rocky outcrops on the coast. "They would be coming across, no doubt, really high levels of the virus in their environment," Fruean said in televised remarks. H5N1 has not shown up in Australia's poultry or agriculture, according to the federal government, which said on Friday that 297 cases have been confirmed nationwide.

item.title: プーチン氏、ウクライナが「パンドラの箱」開けたと非難 報復警告
item.description: [２２日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[２２日　ロイター] - ロシアのプーチン大統領は２２日、ウクライナがロシアの経済施設を攻撃したことで「パンドラの箱」を開けたと非難し、ロシアはウクライナ経済の急所を狙って報復すると警告した。

プーチン氏はロシア国営テレビの記者に対し、「ウクライナはロシア経済に打撃を与えようとし、自らパンドラの箱を開けた。最も脆弱な経済部門を狙う報復を覚悟すべきだ」と発言。ロシアがウクライナ産穀物の輸出分を補えるとして、自国による攻撃が世界的な食料不足を招くことはないとの見方を示した。

ウクライナは今夏、石油精製所やオンライン小売業者の物流施設など、ロシアの経済インフラを標的としたドローン攻撃を強化。ロシアも黒海経由のウクライナ産穀物輸出拠点を含む経済インフラへの攻撃で応酬している。

プーチン氏はまた、ロシアは和平交渉に応じる用意があると改めて表明。ただし、ウクライナが仲介者を通じて提示したという「突飛な」提案ではなく、「現地の現実」を踏まえることが条件だと強調した。

item.title: Alibaba launches $10 billion Hong Kong share placement to fund AI spending
item.description: It would rank as the world's third-largest primary follow-on share sale this year.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: China's Alibaba (9988.HK) on Sunday launched a HK$80-billion ($10.2 billion) share placement to fund artificial intelligence-related development. A deal by the Chinese e-commerce and cloud computing giant would mark the largest-ever primary follow-on offering by a Hong Kong-listed company. It would rank as the world's third-largest primary follow-on share sale this year after offerings from [USN:L4N4291N6 TEXT:"Alphabet"] (GOOGL.O) and [USN:L6N4470KC TEXT:"Intel"] (INTC.O) . The company said it intends to use 100% of the net proceeds from the placement to invest in its "full stack" AI capabilities, a category that includes chips, infrastructure and the development and deployment of AI models. A term sheet reviewed by Reuters showed Alibaba planned to sell 710 million ordinary shares at HK$112.70 a share. That represented a 3.6% discount to its most recent closing price. In its announcement for the $10.2 billion share placement, Alibaba did not reveal additional details on its investment plans by category of its planned AI-related investment. It did not comment beyond its regulatory disclosure. Last week, Alibaba reported its results for the April-to-June quarter, saying it had already spent nearly half of its three-year capex investment plan. It said its expected payback on AI-related investments was on track to fall to 2.5 years from 3 years, driven by surging demand. Alibaba's net profit for the quarter [USN:L4N44H0OB TEXT:"fell 75%"] from a year earlier as it ramped up its AI-related capital expenditures. "In order to be able to capture that future growth, we first need to make these capex investments to build out the necessary compute capacity," CEO Eddie Wu said on an earnings call. The company's share offering has been met with strong demand from investors, including sovereign wealth funds, two people familiar with the deal told Reuters. They could not be named because the information was not public. Alibaba increased the size of the offering after the deal was oversubscribed, the people familiar with the matter said. Morgan Stanley, HSBC, UBS and CICC are serving as joint bookrunners of the Alibaba offering, said one of the sources and a third person with knowledge of the matter. The banks did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. The share placement was not registered under U.S. securities laws as an offshore transaction, meaning American investors were not eligible to participate, Alibaba said. Since 2022, the global AI boom has fuelled staggering capital outlays on infrastructure and data centers, including in the U.S. and China. The four major U.S. hyperscalers - Microsoft (MSFT.O) , Amazon (AMZN.O) , Alphabet (GOOGL.O) and Meta (META.O) - together are expected to spend roughly $725 billion in capital expenditures in 2026, much of it tied to AI data centers, chips and cloud infrastructure. ($1 = 7.8396 Hong Kong dollars)

item.title: ＭＬＢ＝大谷不発もドジャース逆転勝ち、スクバルが加入後初勝利
item.description: ［２２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２２日　ロイター］ - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）は２２日、各地で試合を行い、ドジャースの大谷翔平選手はパイレーツ戦に「１番・指名打者」で出場。３打数ノーヒット、２四球、２三振だった。ドジャースは４─３の逆転勝ちを収めた。

今月トレードでタイガースからドジャースに加入した先発タリク・スクバル投手が７回３失点、１１奪三振と好投。移籍後４試合目の先発で新天地での初勝利を挙げて、今季は８勝７敗となった。

ブルージェイズの岡本和真内野手はヤンキース戦に「５番・三塁」で出場。５打数１安打１得点、２三振だった。ブルージェイズは４─３で勝利した。

カブスの鈴木誠也外野手はマリナーズ戦に「２番・指名打者」で出場し、４打数１安打、１三振。カブスは九回裏に２アウトから３点を奪われ、４─５の逆転サヨナラ負けを喫した。

ホワイトソックスの村上宗隆内野手はメッツ戦に「２番・一塁」で出場。５打数１安打、４三振だった。メッツの千賀滉大投手は５点リードの九回に５番手として登板。１回１安打無失点、１四球、２奪三振だった。試合はメッツが１０─５で勝った。

item.title: サッカー＝昨季王者インテルが開幕戦で快勝、連覇に向けて好発進
item.description: ［ミラノ ２２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［ミラノ　２２日　ロイター］ - サッカーのイタリア・セリエＡは２２日、各地で開幕節を行い、昨季王者インテルがモンツァを４─１で下し、連覇に向けて好発進した。

インテルは前半６分にハカン・チャルハノールがペナルティーエリア外から強烈なシュートを放ち、先制に成功。同２９分に追い付かれたが、後半３分にピオトル・ジエリンスキが勝ち越しゴールを決めると、その後フランチェスコ・エスポジトもヒールキックで加点するなど、快勝を収めた。

昨季２位のナポリはジェノアに２─０で勝利。ケビン・デブルイネらのゴールで終盤に２ゴールを挙げた。

そのほか、カリャリはパルマに１─０で勝利。ウディネーゼとコモは１─１で引き分けた。

item.title: ＭＬＢ＝ブルージェイズのゲレロ、脳震とうから復帰して2安打
item.description: ［２２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２２日　ロイター］　 - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）ブルージェイズのウラジーミル・ゲレロ・ジュニア一塁手（２７）が２２日、負傷者リスト（ＩＬ）から復帰した。

ゲレロは１４日に行われたヤンキース戦の六回、三塁ベースにスライディングした際、相手選手の膝が頭部を直撃。その後、ベンチに下がっていた。同選手は脳震とうで７日間のＩＬに登録されていた。

２２日のヤンキース戦には「２番・一塁」で出場。５打数２安打１得点だった。チームメートの岡本和真内野手は「５番・三塁」で出場し、５打数１安打１得点、２三振。ブルージェイズは４─３で勝利した。

ゲレロは今季、背中やハムストリングのけがを抱えながら１１６試合に出場し、打率２割６分４厘、７本塁打、４６打点の成績。実力を発揮しきれていないが、ジョン・シュナイダー監督は「今でも彼はチームのベストプレーヤーのひとり」とし、「フィジカル的には通常の感覚を取り戻している。彼が本来の状態に戻れることを願っている」と述べた。

同選手は２０日、リハビリのために傘下マイナー１Ａの試合に出場し、適時二塁打１本と２四球を記録。全ての検査で異常はなく、脳震とうプロトコルをクリアしていた。

item.title: ゴルフ＝ＣＰＫＣ女子オープン、山下が単独首位で最終日へ
item.description: ［２２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２２日　ロイター］　 - 米女子ゴルフのＣＰＫＣ女子オープンは２２日、カナダ・エドモントンのロイヤル・メイフェアＧＣ（パー７０）で第３ラウンドを行い、山下美夢有が単独首位をキープした。

山下は６バーディー、１ボギーの５アンダー６５で回り、通算１９アンダーの１９１に伸ばした。６６で回った吉田優利、６４をマークしたジーナ・キム（米国）が６打差の２位につけた。

西郷真央と畑岡奈紗は通算７アンダーの１５位に後退。イーブンパーの７０で回った古江彩佳は通算６アンダーで１２位から２３位に順位を下げた。

岩井千怜は通算４アンダーの３０位。西村優菜は通算３アンダーの３９位となった。

item.title: サッカー＝レアル・マドリード白星発進、バレンシア佐藤がデビュー
item.description: ［バルセロナ ２２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［バルセロナ　２２日　ロイター］ - サッカーのスペイン１部は２２日、各地で試合を行い、ジョゼ・モウリーニョ新監督率いるレアル・マドリードが開幕戦でエスパニョールを２─１で下した。

レアルは前半９分にジュード・ベリンガムのヘディングゴールで先制に成功。同３０分に同点とされたが、後半４５分、その１０分前に投入された新加入のカルロ・エスピが勝ち越し弾をマークした。

今オフにＦＣ東京からバレンシアに移籍した１９歳の日本代表ＭＦ佐藤龍之介は、セルタ戦に先発。新天地でリーグ戦デビューを飾り、後半１２分までプレーした。試合はスコアレスドローだった。

そのほか、セビリアはビルバオに３─１で勝利した。

item.title: ＭＬＢ＝ドジャースのパヘス外野手、左手骨折でＩＬ入り
item.description: ［２２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２２日　ロイター］ - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）のドジャースは２２日、アンディ・パヘス中堅手（２５）を左手の骨折で１０日間の負傷者リスト（ＩＬ）に登録。傘下マイナー３Ａオクラホマシティーからアレク・トーマス中堅手（２６）を昇格させた。

パヘスは２１日に行われたパイレーツ戦の三回の打席で手の甲に死球を受けた。その後もプレーを続けたが、五回の守備で交代していた。

デーブ・ロバーツ監督は試合後、「このようなけがは通常４週間から５週間で治るので、シーズン絶望ではない」とコメント。「彼のことだから、それよりも早く復帰できることに期待している」と話した。

パヘスは今季１２８試合に出場し、打率２割７分２厘、２１本塁打、８０打点。今季初のオールスターに選ばれていた。

今後１カ月間はトーマス、エンリケ・ヘルナンデス一塁手、トミー・エドマン二塁手がパヘスの穴埋めとして、定期的にセンターで起用される見通し。

item.title: Ｆ１＝オランダＧＰ予選で角田12番手、ノリスがＰＰ獲得
item.description: ［ザントフォールト（オランダ） ２２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［ザントフォールト（オランダ）　２２日　ロイター］ - 自動車レースＦ１のオランダ・グランプリ（ＧＰ）は２２日、予選を行い、リアム・ローソン（ニュージーランド）のレッドブル昇格を受けてレーシングブルズから出場している角田裕毅は１２番手だった。

昨季総合王者ランド・ノリス（英国、マクラーレン）が２戦連続のポールポジション（ＰＰ）を獲得した。２０２１年以来、オランダＧＰではＰＰを獲得したドライバーが毎年優勝している。

ジョージ・ラッセル（英国）が２番手、総合首位のキミ・アントネッリ（イタリア）が３番手とメルセデス勢が続き、ノリスの同僚オスカー・ピアストリ（オーストラリア）が４番手だった。

通算７回の総合優勝を誇るルイス・ハミルトン（英国、フェラーリ）は５番手、チームメートのシャルル・ルクレール（モナコ）は６番手、マックス・フェルスタッペン（オランダ、レッドブル）が７番手、ローソンは８番手。レーシングブルズのもう１台、アービッド・リンドブラッド（英国）は１０番手だった。

予選の前に行われたスプリント決勝ではラッセルが優勝し、ルクレールが２位、ノリスが３位、アントネッリが４位、ピアストリが５位、フェルスタッペンが６位、ハミルトンが７位。リンドブラッドは１０位、ローソンは１１位、角田は１３位だった。

item.title: サッカー＝ドイツ・スーパー杯、バイエルンがドルトムント下す
item.description: ［ドルトムント（ドイツ） ２２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［ドルトムント（ドイツ）　２２日　ロイター］ - サッカーのドイツ・スーパーカップ（杯）は２２日に試合を行い、昨季国内リーグとドイツ杯で優勝したバイエルン・ミュンヘンが、リーグ２位のドルトムントを２─１で下した。

バイエルンは前半２８分、ミカエル・オリーズのお膳立てから新加入のナサニエル・ブラウンが先制点をマーク。同アディショナルタイム１分には、相手陣内でボールを持ったオリーズがそのままドリブルで持ち上がり、チームの２点目を記録した。

ドルトムントは後半３０分にファビオ・シルバが１点を返したが、同４５分にレッドカードで１人を失い、追い付くことはできなかった。バイエルンの伊藤洋輝はベンチ入りしたが出場はなかった。

バイエルンのバンサン・コンパニ監督は「この勝利に非常に満足している」とコメント。「昨季は全てを制したので、今季は勢いが落ちるだろうと思う人もいるかもしれないが、そうはならない。われわれは気を緩めず、全てを手にしたいと思っている」と話した。

item.title: ゴルフ＝ＢＭＷ選手権で久常8位に浮上、松山は43位に後退
item.description: ［２２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２２日　ロイター］ - 米男子ゴルフのプレーオフ第２戦、ＢＭＷ選手権は２２日、ミズーリ州セントルイスのベルリーブＣＣ（パー７０）で第３ラウンドを行い、久常涼は８位に浮上した。

前日１６位だった久常は７バーディー、４ボギーの３アンダー６７でラウンド。通算８アンダーの２０２とした。３７位で出た松山英樹は７０で回り、通算イーブンパーの４３位に後退した。

今年の全米オープン選手権で優勝したウィンダム・クラーク（米国）が１イーグル、６バーディー、１ダブルボギー、１ボギーの５アンダー６５をマーク。通算１７アンダーに伸ばし、単独首位をキープした。

世界ランキング２位のロリー・マキロイ（英国）、今季初優勝を目指すパトリック・カントレー（米国）が５打差の２位で並んでいる。世界１位のスコッティ・シェフラー（米国）は通算５アンダーの１５位。

item.title: サッカー＝昇格組のイプスウィッチ白星スタート、前田が先発出場
item.description: ［２２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded: ［２２日　ロイター］　 - サッカーのイングランド・プレミアリーグは２２日、開幕節を行い、前田大然が所属する昇格組のイプスウィッチはサンダーランドに２─１で勝利した。セルティック（スコットランド）から加入した前田は先発し、後半３５分までプレーした。鎌田大地と冨安健洋が所属するクリスタルパレスはエバートンに０─２で敗れた。鎌田はフル出場。冨安は後半２７分から出場した。田中碧が所属するリーズはノッティンガム・フォレストに１─０で勝利。田中はベンチ入りしたが、出番はなかった。１０年ぶりのプレミア昇格を果たしたハルはマンチェスター・ユナイテッド（マンＵ）を２─０で下した。ハルがリーグ戦でマンＵに勝ったのは５２年ぶりで、マンＵが開幕戦で昇格組に負けたのはこれが初めて。ハルの守田英正はベンチ外だった。トットナムはブレントフォードに０─３で完敗。トットナムの高井幸大はメンバー入りしなかった。

item.title: カナダ、対米報復関税を9月8日発動へ 鉄鋼や電子機器など対象
item.description:
Promit Mukherjee Bhargav Acharya
[オタワ ２２日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Promit Mukherjee　Bhargav Acharya

[オタワ ２２日 ロイター] - カナダのカーニー首相は２２日、トランプ米政権がカナダ製品に５０％の追加関税を発動したことへの報復として、９月８日から米国産の鉄鋼、電子機器、その他の製品に対して関税を課すと表明した。

米国は２２日、カナダとの通商交渉が物別れに終わったことを受け、約２００億ドル相当のカナダ製品に５０％の追加関税を発動した。

カナダによる関税は米側の措置と金額ベースで同規模となる。

カーニー氏は記者会見で「カナダの労働者、農家、家庭、企業を守るため、米国による新たな関税に同規模で対抗する」と述べた。貿易戦争に突入したのかとの質問に対しては「攻撃されたら、それは戦争だ。われわれは攻撃された」と応じた。

米国産の鉄鋼、乳製品、家電、農業機械、パルプ・紙、電子機器に加え、米国がこれまでにカナダを対象として関税を課してきた品目の一部にも関税を課すと説明した。

グリア米通商代表部（ＵＳＴＲ）代表は２２日、ＦＯＸニュースに対し、交渉決裂について「カナダは米国と協力する機会を逃した」とし、新たな協議は予定されていないと述べた。

また「われわれはカナダの報復に対応する措置を進めている」とし、「カナダは常に最良の条件を得てきたし、さらに良い条件も得られたはずだが、それを望まなかった」と述べた。

カーニー氏は「米国が示した条件は受け入れられず、彼らの要求に応じることもない」と述べた。

トランプ米大統領は２１日、カナダと同日中に合意できると期待を示していた。

しかしカーニー氏は、米側による土壇場での要求が進展を阻んだと説明。「ここ数日に米国は経済的に不合理で不公平、かつカナダの国益を損なう新たな条件を提示し、合意の信頼性に疑念を生じさせた」とし、要求にはカナダが新たな貿易協定を結ぶ能力を制限する内容が含まれていたと述べた。

カーニー氏は米国の新関税で打撃を受ける産業への支援策を来週にも発表する方針も示し、これらの措置は数年にわたる可能性があるとした。

米国の関税に強く反対してきたオンタリオ州のフォード首相は、カーニー氏が報復を決定したことに支持を表明。「カーニー首相が合意に署名しなくて良かった。悪い合意だったからだ。オンタリオ州にとっても、自動車、鉄鋼、製造業にとっても悪い合意だった」と記者団に語った。

主要な争点の一つは大型車両の扱いだった。複数の関係者によると、カナダは小型車向けに提案された有利な関税条件を中・大型トラックにも拡大するよう求めたが、米側は難色を示した。カーニー氏によると、米国の立場では、フォード・モーターの「Ｆ－３５０」「Ｆ－４５０」「Ｆ－５５０」トラックやゼネラル・モーターズ（ＧＭ）の「シルバラード」といったカナダ製モデルが除外されることになり、カナダでの生産の競争力が損なわれる恐れがあったという。

カーニー氏は、米側の提案にはカナダの文化、言語、主権に関わる内容も含まれていたと述べたが、詳細には触れなかった。

item.title: Iran condemns US plans to announce new sanctions
item.description: The sanctions could put further strain on Iran's economy and have an impact on its most important trading partners, including China.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

World

Iran condemns US plans to announce new sanctions

The sanctions could put further strain on Iran's economy and have an impact on its most important trading partners, including China.

An Iranian missile system is displayed in Azadi Square in Tehran on Jul 30, 2026. (File photo: Reuters/WANA/Majid Asgaripour)

FAST

CAIRO: Iran on Saturday (Aug 22) denounced United States plans to announce new sanctions that could put further strain on the Islamic Republic's economy and have an impact on its most important trading partners, including China. After nearly six months of war since the US and Israel launched airstrikes against Iran on Feb 28, the sides are not firing at each other but also showing no sign of pursuing peace talks. Oil shipments are at a virtual standstill in the Strait of Hormuz , with Tehran threatening to strike any unauthorised oil tankers that try to transit the vital waterway, and Iran's economy is already under immense pressure from sanctions. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is due to hold a press conference at 2pm (6pm GMT) on Monday after threatening "the toughest sanctions in history" on Iran.

Commentary: For Iran’s new leaders, peace is more dangerous than war

Bessent has also urged cooperation with Washington by China, which buys more than 80 per cent of Iran's shipped oil, according to 2025 data from analytics firm Kpler. Beijing has urged diplomacy. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson, Esmaeil Baghaei, said on Saturday the imminent US announcement of new economic sanctions was an "assertion of extraterritorial sovereignty over every independent member state of the United Nations". "Such secondary sanctions find no foundation in international law," he said in a post on X. The secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, Mohsen Rezaei, told state television that Tehran would target the interests of countries helping the United States. "We are telling all nearby countries not to join the US economic war, otherwise we will consider them as enemies," Rezaei said. US President Donald Trump, who has warned of economic consequences against any country that provides "any type of lifeline to Iran", said on Friday that Washington was observing "what happens" in the conflict. "They would love to make a deal, but they're not ready to make the right deal, in my opinion," Trump said of Iran.

Related:

Iran threatens to go on offensive in Strait of Hormuz if diplomacy with US fails

HORMUZ TRAFFIC HALTED While the US has effectively blockaded Iranian vessels in their ports, the Strait of Hormuz remained bottled up with thousands of seafarers stranded on hundreds of vessels. Only four commodity ships sailed along the strait on Thursday, none of them large crude carriers or liquefied natural gas tankers ship-tracking data showed. However, Iran has granted permission for a number of raqi oil tankers to pass through the Strait following repeated requests from Baghdad, Iran's state news agency IRNA reported on Saturday. IRNA said obtaining special permission for Iraqi tankers was one of Baghdad’s main requests during a visit to Iraq by Parliament speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said the US military helped move a seven-day average of 8 million barrels a day of oil through the strait. That's down from more than 20 million per day before the war, or about one of every five barrels consumed worldwide. US attacks have severely diminished Iran's economy and devastated its navy and air force, but Tehran maintains enough missile and drone capability to impede oil tanker traffic and attack regional rivals. Abdollahi, the armed forces chief of staff, sought to underline Iran's missile capabilities during a visit to an underground plant manufacturing ballistic missiles that was reported by state television on Saturday. "This plant has been able, much better than in the past, to produce equipment superior both in capacities and quality and in quantity," he said. Qalibaf, Iran's parliamentary speaker, said Tehran had received "numerous messages" from neighbouring countries about establishing new regional security arrangements and economic cooperation. Qalibaf, who did not say which countries he was referring to, accused the US of endangering the security of its allies in the region for the sake of Israel, adding that an independent, "homegrown" regional order would deliver peace and security. Trump, meanwhile, has yet to achieve objectives he set at the start of the war, such as dismantling Iran's nuclear programme - the state of which remains uncertain given that UN inspectors have been shut out since 2025 - and creating conditions for Iranians to overthrow their clerical rulers. Thousands have been killed, mainly in Iran, where 168 Iranian school children were killed on the first day of the war. The US has reported more than 750 military personnel wounded and 18 killed. While Iran remains defiant, President Masoud Pezeshkian has also called for a diplomatic solution. "It would be better to end the war today, when we are powerful and have dignity, and the whole world acknowledges our victory and emphasises that America, contrary to all regulations, attacked our schools, hospitals and infrastructure and is hated in the world," the ISNA news agency quoted him as saying on Friday.

Source: Reuters/fs/kg

Some of Nvidia's largest customers have been told prices of servers containing its artificial intelligence chips will rise by more than 15 per cent in many cases, with memory chip costs soaring, Bloomberg News reported on Saturday (Aug 22). The price hikes will go into effect on systems shipped early next year and will impact systems including those with the flagship Vera Rubin and Grace Blackwell chips, the report added, citing people familiar with the process. The increases will depend on Nvidia's chip generation and memory configurations, they said. Reuters could not immediately verify the report. Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comments outside regular business hours. Companies that build servers under contract for large data centre operators such as Microsoft, Alphabet's Google and Oracle have recently informed their customers of the upcoming increases, the report added. Nvidia, whose chips underpin much of the AI infrastructure buildout, is set to report second-quarter results on Aug 26. The company has become a proxy for the broader AI ecosystem spanning chipmakers and companies financing the rapid expansion of data centre capacity.

item.title: EU sends helicopters, firefighters to Serbia to tackle wildfires
item.description: Serbia has struggled for weeks with a wildfire in a unique mixture of sand dunes and woods.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The European Union’s Civil Protection Mechanism sent helicopters and firefighters to help Serbia fight a massive wildfire in a nature reserve in the northeast of the country, the head of the EU mission to Belgrade said on Saturday. Serbia activated the mechanism on Friday after struggling for weeks with a wildfire in Deliblatska Pescara, a unique mixture of sand dunes and woods about 80 km (50 miles) from the capital Belgrade, as well as other blazes in the southwest of the country. “We stand with Serbia in protecting lives, livelihoods and the unique natural heritage of Deliblatska Sands,” Andreas Beckerath, the head of the EU mission to Belgrade, wrote on X. Luka Causic, the head of the Serbian Department for Emergencies, said that European aid consists of four Black Hawk firefighting helicopters from Romania, Slovakia and the Czech Republic, 55 firefighters and 24 vehicles from Germany, and 69 firefighters and 15 vehicles from Romania. One helicopter from Romania and one from Slovakia joined firefighting efforts on Saturday, while two others from the Czech Republic will be engaged on Sunday, Serbia's Interior Ministry said in a statement. Romanian firefighters and vehicles have also arrived in the town od Bela Crkva, near the fire. A German team is expected to arrive on August 24, it said. Serbia is not a member of the EU but has access to emergency EU help under its Civil Protection Mechanism. This summer, Belgrade sent a firefighting helicopter and emergency response team to help Spain combat wildfires after repeated blazes across Europe sapped EU resources. [USN:L1N44H0A9 TEXT:"A Russian"] Emergencies Ministry IL-76P firefighting plane landed in the southern Serbian city of Nis on Wednesday to tackle the Deliblatska Pescara wildfire, which has gutted thousands of hectares of pine forest since late July. Causic said the situation was more stable on Saturday, but that strong winds were expected and the priority is to protect settlements and human lives. Other major wildfires were also active in the rugged Stolovi mountain range in the southwest of the country. In neighbouring North Macedonia, a major wildfire was raging in the municipality of Strumica, south of the capital Skopje. According to media reports, at least one house caught fire in the village of Sofilar.

STOCKHOLM: Swedish police are investigating whether an 18-year-old man who attacked students at a Swedish high school with a sword on Friday (Aug 21), killing one, was involved in online communities promoting school violence, a police source said. The attacker struck at a school in the central Swedish town of Fagersta, also severely injuring two teenage boys before being arrested by police. The parents of a 17-year-old girl told local newspaper Fagersta-Posten that their daughter was killed in the attack. Police are investigating whether a TikTok account that posted a picture of a sword 20 minutes before the assault belonged to the suspect, the source told Reuters. According to the Dagens Nyheter newspaper, the image appeared to have been taken in a restroom at the school. Before it was taken down on Friday, the month-old account contained videos that referred to two mass violence attacks in Sweden and to Norwegian far-right mass murderer Anders Behring Breivik. It also referenced a 2015 attack, where a masked swordsman killed a teaching assistant and two boys at a school in Trollhattan, western Sweden, before being shot dead by police. "The investigators are looking into various online communities which might have egged on the suspect to carry out the attack," the police source said. Prosecutors on Saturday ordered the man's detention on suspicion of murder and several counts of attempted murder. "The investigation is at an intense stage. We are conducting interrogations and gathering information, but I cannot go into specifics," Prosecutor Ann-Sofie Trossing told Reuters.

item.title: Chinese robots beat Usain Bolt's 100m world record at Beijing games
item.description: A Chinese humanoid robot ran 100 metres in 9.39 seconds in a preliminary heat at the World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing on Saturday, faster than the men's world record held by Jamaican sprinting great Usain Bolt.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Baptista, Qiaoyi Li
item.content:encoded: A Chinese humanoid robot ran 100 metres in 9.39 seconds in a preliminary heat at the World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing on Saturday, faster than the men's world record held by Jamaican sprinting great Usain Bolt. Tiangong Ultra, developed by the Beijing Humanoid Robot Innovation Center, won its heat at the opening of the games' second edition, organisers said. The robot overtook smartphone maker Honor's Lightning near the finish after falling behind early in the race. Lightning finished in 9.47 seconds, also faster than the 9.58-second record Bolt set at the 2009 World Athletics Championships in Berlin. The two robots lacked Bolt's flair, slamming straight into a thick mat designed to stop them in their tracks, with Tiangong stumbling wildly into the sidelines, forcing onlookers to move out of the way. Lightning was carried away on a stretcher after collapsing to the ground. The results nevertheless marked a sharp improvement from last year's inaugural games, when Tiangong Ultra won the 100 metres in 21.50 seconds. Tiangong also won the world's first humanoid robot half-marathon, held in Beijing last year. Earlier on Saturday, Chinese state media reported that Lightning had run 100 metres in 9.32 seconds in a preparatory test, reaching a peak speed of 14.5 metres per second. Lightning won this year's humanoid half-marathon in 50 minutes and 26 seconds, faster than the pace of the elite men's human world record. Lightning stood 169 cm tall and had 95-cm legs during the half-marathon. Its researchers later lengthened its legs by 10 cm, to 1.05 metres, ahead of the games, according to broadcaster CCTV. The 100 metres is among 51 events at the games, which include football, dancing and industrial-task contests. CHINA SEES HUMANOID ROBOTS AS STRATEGIC INDUSTRY China has promoted humanoid robots as a strategic emerging industry, with policymakers and companies betting that advances in AI and hardware will accelerate their use in manufacturing, logistics and consumer applications. Investor enthusiasm for the sector was on display earlier this week when shares in Unitree, China's best-known humanoid robot maker, [USN:L1N44G01S TEXT:"jumped more than five fold"] in its Shanghai trading debut on Wednesday, giving the company a market value of about $50 billion. This year's games have drawn 2,056 robots from 666 teams across 16 countries and six continents, up from 280 teams at the inaugural event. The games, held at Beijing's National Speed Skating Oval, run through Wednesday.

LAHORE: The party of Pakistan's jailed ex-prime minister Imran Khan filed a contempt petition against the government on Saturday (Aug 22) after authorities took the cricketer-turned-politician to a state-run hospital instead of the private facility ordered by the top court, party officials said.  "The petition seeks action against the prime minister, law minister, information minister" and other government officials, said Naeem Panjutha, a legal advisor for Khan's party, Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), adding it also calls for Khan's treatment at the private hospital ordered by the court.  Khan, who remains highly popular in Pakistan, has been imprisoned since August 2023 on charges he calls politically motivated after a fallout with the country's powerful military led to his removal from office. His arrest sparked massive nationwide protests, including the storming of military installations, and public perception that he was moved back to jail forcefully has the potential to rekindle such demonstrations.  A three-judge bench on Tuesday directed the government to transfer Khan from Adiala Jail to the private Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad within two days for medical examination.

Officials instead took Khan to the state-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) overnight on Friday for a brief check-up before returning him to jail and did not give him access to his personal physician, which the party also cites as a breach of court orders.  The PTI interprets the order as requiring Khan to remain under medical supervision until at least mid-September. Khan’s sister, Uzma Khan, who attended the examination at PIMS, told media that while her brother is physically fit, “Khan told me that he is being repeatedly tortured in prison”. The interior and law ministries as well as jail authorities have not responded to a request for comment from Reuters on the allegations of torture. Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said on Friday Khan was examined at PIMS because of security risks.  Khan's supporters had lined Islamabad streets overnight, and PTI leaders say the episode will intensify pressure and boost preparations for a planned protest march on September 27.

South Korea container ship sets sail to test Arctic commercial route amid Western concerns

President Lee Jae Myung has made Arctic shipping a priority for South Korea, a shipping powerhouse.

The PanStar Acro, a container ship bound for Europe via the Arctic, testing whether a route opened by melting sea ice can be commercially viable, is anchored at a port in Busan, South Korea, August 20, 2026. Yonhap via REUTERS

SEOUL: A South Korean container ship sets sail on Saturday (Aug 22) for Europe via the Arctic in the nation's first commercial voyage on the route to test its viability, with the hope of turning the southeastern port of Busan into a global maritime hub. The PanStar Acro will sail north, hugging eastern Russia's Kamchatka peninsula, cross the Bering Sea, and take the Northern Sea Route, stopping in Felixstowe in Britain, Rotterdam in the Netherlands and Poland's Gdansk before returning on a journey expected to take 40 to 45 days. President Lee Jae Myung has made Arctic shipping a priority for South Korea, a shipping powerhouse. Officials say this could help transform Busan and position the Arctic as a regular trade route by 2030. But the project risks friction with Western allies hoping to keep Russia isolated during its war in Ukraine. Seoul has consulted with Moscow about the journey, including whether the ship needed help to tackle any problems, such as getting stuck in ice.

Last year, 88 vessels made 103 transits through the route, up from 97 in 2024 and 43 in 2022, chiefly from nations such as Russia and China, according to Norway's Centre for High North Logistics. Melting Arctic ice has made passage through the north easier, while the increased shipping in turn accelerates global warming, scientists say. The 2,758 TEU (Twenty-Foot Equivalent Unit) container ship operated by South Korea's PanStar has secured 837 TEU of cargo including auto parts, chemical products and about 100 empty containers on the government-backed voyage. The PanStar Acro is scheduled to flag off at around 8pm (11am GMT) depending on loading and preparations, a government official said.
